Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a chemical cross-linking (CXMS) study using the BMOE crosslinker to identify dimerization interfaces of the AR-LBD. While not a traditional 'enrichment' for a PTM, it targets the complexome/protein-protein interaction. Base workflow is DDA LFQ as no labeling is mentioned.

scope: Recombinant human AR-LBD (residues 662–919) was expressed as a fusion protein with thioredoxin and purified to homogeneity using standard purification methods.
Coomassie Brilliant Blue-stained bands corresponding to monomeric and dimeric AR-LBD were excised from the gels and subjected to in-gel digestion following standard protocols.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on purified recombinant AR-LBD protein (monomers and dimers) excised from SDS-PAGE gels. While the paper discusses nuclear localization in cell-based FRET assays, the material actually analyzed by LC-MS/MS was the purified recombinant protein.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment specifically uses chemical cross-linking (BMOE) to differentiate between monomeric and dimeric states of the AR-LBD for MS analysis. While the broader study discusses disease mutations and ligand stimulation, those were analyzed via FRET and transactivation assays, not the MS-analyzed samples. The MS analysis is a structural validation of the dimer interface.
